claims.title: Data satisfying the cell condition give both breakdown conclusions

passages.quote:
The Lean package proves that data satisfying `CellSystemCondition` give
blow-up on $\mathbb R^3$ and on $\mathbb T^3$.

comparisons.note: The theorem gives both whole-space and torus breakdown under the complete cell condition. This is the conditional implication stated in the opening sentence.
The condition is the fifteen-clause premise of that implication. A numerical witness satisfying it is a separate obligation.

passages.quote: `CellSystemCondition` has fifteen fields over seven data arguments.

comparisons.note: The condition has fifteen direct clauses over the seven shared choices of cell data, field instances, local calculations, tree, assembly, constants and reduction data. The sentence counts these choices correctly.

passages.quote:
**Quadratic forms are required on a larger space than the cell's
coordinates.** `InRowRange` ([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:6547`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6547)) constrains only
the coordinates whose row reason is not `.unused`, and only up to gauge and
pressure-head terms with complex coefficients; unused coordinates and port
coordinates are free complex numbers; the two actuator blocks are free real
numbers.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: Only used row coordinates are constrained by the common real row variables and complex gauge and pressure-head terms. All unused and port coordinates are free complex numbers, and both actuator blocks are required to be real.

passages.quote:
The local estimates in `PotentialConditions.kept_le`,
`PairingConditions.kept_le` and `EliminationConditions.residual_value_le`
must hold for every such vector.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The retained potential inequality is quantified over every vector satisfying the supplied admissibility condition. In the final cell condition that is the complete compatible-row space described immediately before this sentence.
The retained pairing inequality is quantified over every admissible vector. Substituting the final compatible-row condition gives the full domain stated in the passage.
The residual elimination comparison is quantified over every admissible vector. It therefore includes the free and gauge directions of the full compatible-row condition.

passages.quote:
**Missing table entries need the right continuation, which is not always
zero.** For sparse spline and jet coefficients, `VanishesBeyond`
([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:6853`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6853)) reads an out-of-range breakpoint as the
support radius, which makes its guard true, so every coefficient past the
stored list must be exactly zero.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The missing-breakpoint default R makes each affected support guard true because R ≤ |R|. A node coefficient needs one guard and a bubble coefficient needs both endpoint guards; when both endpoints are absent, the bubble coefficient is therefore forced to zero.

passages.quote:
`actuator_model_regular`
([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:6050`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6050)) quantifies over every natural index, not
only those below the number of actuators.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The actuator-model measurability and weighted-square-integrability condition quantifies over every natural index. It is broader than a check restricted to the finitely many physical actuators.

passages.quote:
**Scales may be zero.** `ScaledJetAxis.convert`
([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:4140`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4140)) inverts `scale.getD k 1`, and
`HasSymmetricScale` requires only the right length and symmetry.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The node conversion uses the inverse scale with missing scales replaced by 1. Its formula remains defined at scale zero, as the passage says.
The scale condition requires equality of list lengths and invariance under reversal. It does not require any scale to be nonzero.

passages.quote:
**Active harmonics can be over-approximated instead of decided.**
`modelLabels` ([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:5753`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5753)) keeps a label when some model
coefficient is nonzero somewhere on the cell, and its three users
(`group_link`, `groups_cover`, `rows_groups_cover`) demand coverage for every
kept label.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: A label is active when it belongs to one of the four model supports and some component is nonzero at a point in the cell. The definition directly supports conservative coverage by all declared supports.
The coupling-group conditions require coverage for active labels and their unresolved partners. Checking the same coverage for every declared support label is sufficient for these clauses.
The tested-row coverage condition quantifies over active model labels. It is the third consumer of the active-label set identified in the sentence.

passages.quote:
**Mode triples must be distinct.** `AzimuthalBounded`
([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:3576`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3576)) asks for an injective family of
(component, frequency, order) triples.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The harmonic expansion requires the component, temporal-frequency and azimuthal-order triples to be distinct. This is the exact orthogonality requirement stated in the passage.

passages.quote:
`IsBoxUniform.bounds_eq`
transports the support object across the parameter set.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The full bounding data are equal to their central value for every parameter in K. This transports the harmonic supports and all associated bounds together.

passages.quote:
On this path
`AdjointEntryLinks.fitted_empty` ([`CellLayerChallenge.lean:4022`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4022)) makes the
fitted adjoint set empty, so the fitted bounds hold vacuously.

anchor.heading: 2. Where a natural implementation checks too little

comparisons.note: The fitted-direction set is empty for every selected adjoint. All bounds quantified over that set are therefore vacuous on this specialised route.

passages.quote:
Much of the infinite and analytic content is proved in Lean, with finite data
as input: the extension of checked finite bases to infinite orthonormal ones,
spline joins and scaled-jet facts, the logarithmic radial phase, step-phase
regularity, pressure continuity and periodicity, the moved profile and adjoint
constructions, potential-series derivatives and decay, and the azimuthal dual
estimate (`AdjointDefect.remainderAzimuthalHolds_proof`).

anchor.heading: 3. What the library already proves, and what it takes as input

comparisons.note: The linked theorem supplies the azimuthal dual estimate by combining the angular inverse-square bound, approximation, mode pairing and time orthogonality. The earlier representation results listed in the sentence are separate results.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceAndTorusB.text: The guide states the complete cell-condition implication: satisfying the fifteen conditions gives both whole-space and torus breakdown. The statement itself supplies no numerical data satisfying those conditions.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
